claim_summary: ElliottAgents is a fixed seven-agent pipeline that detects Elliott Wave patterns in stock prices, validates them with DRL backtesting against stored historical outcomes, and synthesizes forecasts into trading recommendations.

claim_evidence.quote: This paper introduces ElliottAgents, an multi-agent system that integrates the Elliott Wave Principle with AI for stock market forecasting.

modules.name: Coordinator-managed multi-agent execution flow
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 no: the coordinator, hierarchical roles, asynchronous parallel execution, task decomposition and memory identifiers (Sec. 4.5) do not embed a task objective or verifier; the stock-specific stage order is an instantiation of the flow, not the mechanism. R3_2 no: no temporal semantics. R3_3 yes: scheduling, delegation and state passing between agents.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - coordination mechanism has no task objective
R3_3_GH:yes - coordinator scheduling, parallel execution and state

evidence.quote: The Coordinator agent orchestrates the entire process. It begins by receiving user input, including the desired stock symbol and analysis timeframe.
The coordinator is the agent who manages the whole flow of information in the system, distributes the tasks and ensures their execution, as presented on Fig. 6.
Asynchronous task execution enables agents to operate in parallel, mitigating bottlenecks and enhancing throughput (Li et al., 2024).

modules.name: Elliott-wave detection and chart tools
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 no: the Elliott-wave reader identifies and classifies wave structure in ordered price series and feeds both the forecast and the advice; it carries no output requirement or verifier of either task family, so replacing the task does not force a redesign. R3_2 yes: detection depends on temporal order and multiple timeframes (daily, hourly).
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - detector has no task objective
R3_2_GTS:yes - wave detection over ordered series and timeframes

evidence.quote: The platform implements algorithms for identifying Elliott Wave patterns across multiple timeframes as a tool for agents. Then results of this tool are interpreted by LLM-based agents.
Elliot waves reader: tool for technical analysis, helping the agent identify and interpret Elliot wave patterns in price movements.

modules.name: DRL backtesting of wave patterns with stored outcome reuse
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 yes: the Backtester validates detected wave patterns against historical price outcomes with a DRL model and stores pattern-outcome records for later forecasts; its reward, verifier and stored state are defined by the price-prediction objective and would be redesigned for another task family. The DRL model is separate from the LLM, so it is Harness, not LLM side. The knowledge-base lookup and storage only function inside this procedure, so they are merged here.
rubric_path: R2:Harness (DRL model is separate from the LLM)
R3_1_TSK:yes - validates forecasts against historical outcomes
R4:Tools and Execution; Memory and Context; Optimization and Evolution

evidence.quote: The Backtester agent then receives the identified patterns and employs DRL to validate them against historical trends, assessing their effectiveness.
The Backtester’s workflow begins with a query to determine if relevant results are already available in the backtesting knowledge base.
These findings are then stored in the Neo4j graph database for future reference.

modules.name: Investment-strategy synthesis with price targets and stop-loss
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 yes: the Investment Advisor procedure embeds the decision output requirement (buy/sell/hold, entry and exit price targets, stop-loss, time frames); another decision task needs a different output and risk criterion. The generic orchestration moved to multi-agent-workflow.

- Buy, sell, or hold recommendations - Price targets for entry and exit points - Stop-loss levels - Time frames for the transactions

task_performance.quote: The second phase of our experimentation was designed to assess the system’s pattern recognition capabilities and the accuracy of its predictions.

decision_utility.quote: we could simulate transactions and calculate theoretical investment returns, proving the effectiveness of predictions of future prices.

reconciliation.reason: The detector has no task objective and depends on temporal order and timeframes; it serves both forecasting and advice. Same mechanism, id kept.

changes: dimensions: Coordination and Scaling, Planning and Workflow, Interface and Interaction -> Planning and Orchestration
generic coordinator/parallel-execution mechanism moved to new GH module multi-agent-workflow
reconciliation.reason: The card merged the Coordinator-managed flow (Sec. 4.5) with the Advisor's decision output. Orchestration has no task objective (GH); the Advisor prompt does (TSK).

items.reason: The Coordinator runs a predetermined agent order (data, waves, backtest, expert, advisor, report); the only conditional is the backtest knowledge-base lookup, which does not change the action sequence of the agents.
The wave reader identifies structure in ordered price series across timeframes and has no forecasting or advice output requirement; its output serves both task families.
Coordinator, hierarchy, asynchronous execution and memory identifiers (L430-L450) are task-neutral scheduling; the Advisor prompt (L353-L371) embeds buy/sell/stop-loss outputs.

items.item: Codex agent-workflow as TSK vs Haiku multi-agent-workflow as GH
items.reason: R3_3 applies: the mechanism described in Sec. 4.5 does not embed a task objective; the stock stage order is only its instance.

items.item: DRL backtester and backtest knowledge store (Haiku: TSK + GTS; Codex: one TSK)
items.reason: Sec. 4.4 describes the lookup, analysis and storage as one Backtester workflow whose records are forecasting pattern outcomes; the store has no cutoff or availability logic, so it does not stand alone as GTS.
The quoted wave non-overlap rule is a pattern definition, not a chronological split, leakage control or availability check; the cross-validation split is not described as chronological.
The Advisor prompt synthesizes text outputs and implements none of the four temporal functions.

adjudication.summary: Role is a fixed workflow; the wave reader is GTS, orchestration is GH, and the DRL backtester with its knowledge store and the investment synthesis are TSK. Temporal validity evidence was removed.

notes: GPT-4o-mini is used unchanged (L463) and fine-tuning is avoided (L419-L420), so no LLM-side module. Reuse for the workflow and wave reader rests on one stock pipeline serving two families (module tasks), a judgment call. Table 1 is garbled in the extraction.
